overview: This lecture introduces what an **operating system** is and does, covering computer-system structure, the roles of the **kernel**, system programs, and middleware. It explains how hardware components interact through **interrupts**, I/O handling, DMA, and the storage hierarchy. It also covers OS operations such as multiprogramming, multitasking, and **dual-mode operation** for protecting the system.
questions: How does an interrupt work, and what role does the interrupt vector play in handling it?
What is the difference between multiprogramming and multitasking (timesharing)?
How does dual-mode operation use the mode bit and system calls to keep user programs from running privileged instructions?
